resolution: All 10 findings independently reproduced by the producer and applied to plan.md; no unresolved findings.

findings.claim: c300 task 3 orders restoring .kimi/, but openspec 1.10.0 MIGRATES .kimi -> .kimi-code; restoring recreates what the tool deletes each run, making the idempotence criterion unsatisfiable.
findings.evidence: openspec update --force on a clean git-archive HEAD tree prints 'Migrated 10 skills: .kimi -> .kimi-code'; .kimi openspec dirs -> 0, .kimi-code -> 10.
findings.status: REPRODUCED — applied. c300 now accepts the migration and drops .kimi from the harness list.

findings.claim: c300 task 2 ('bring .codex to 1.10.0') has no mechanism: .codex is not in the project's OpenSpec tool set.
findings.evidence: Same run reports 'Force updating 4 tool(s): claude, kimi, opencode, agents' and touches .codex zero times.
findings.status: REPRODUCED — applied. c300 task 2 is now a decision (manage via openspec init --tools codex, or drop from the harness list) that blocks task 3.

findings.claim: c304's grep-based criterion is unsatisfiable: the W6.x sequences are offset by one across W6.6-W6.9, not disagreeing on a single label.
findings.evidence: docs/03:191 W6.7=prom-hook-dispatch, :222 W6.8=sessionstart matchers; docs/05:596 W6.8=prom-hook-dispatch, :597 W6.9=sessionstart matchers.
findings.status: REPRODUCED — applied. c304 now renumbers a whole sequence and adds a mechanical mapping check with a negative fixture.

findings.claim: audit.sh has no layer-contract mode and exits 0 for ANY unrecognised mode, so the gate inventory counts a non-existent check and any criterion invoking audit.sh <mode> can pass by typo.

findings.status: REPRODUCED — applied. c300 task 8 makes unknown modes fail; the stale warning is corrected.
